The must-sees

  • Bordeaux Cathedral

    Church

    In 1137 Eleanor of Aquitaine married the future Louis VII of France here. It is part of the UNESCO-listed routes to Santiago de Compostela.

    Look for: Beside the cathedral stands a separate bell tower, the Tour Pey-Berland. It is said to have been set apart so the bells would not shake the church.

  • Bordeaux Quays

    Waterfront

    The crescent bend of the river gave the city its nickname, the Port of the Moon. It was listed by UNESCO in 2007.

    Look for: Downstream, the Pont Jacques Chaban-Delmas has four tall pylons; its middle span lifts straight up to let ships pass.

  • Grand Théâtre

    Culture · 1780

    Victor Louis designed it, and it opened in 1780. It is still the home of the Bordeaux opera and ballet.

    Look for: Count the statues along the roofline: twelve, the nine Muses joined by the goddesses Juno, Venus and Minerva.

  • La Cité du Vin

    Museum · 2016

    It opened in 2016 in the former docks north of the centre. The top-floor belvedere looks out across the river and the city.

    Look for: The skin of glass and shimmering metal panels shifts colour with the light and the river.

  • Place de la Bourse

    Square

    It was designed by Jacques Gabriel and completed by his son Ange-Jacques in the mid-1700s. The Three Graces fountain stands at its centre.

    Look for: The palace on the south side was built for the tax collectors and now holds France’s national customs museum.

  • Place des Quinconces

    Square

    The square was laid out in the early 19th century on the site of a demolished fortress. The monument honours the Girondin deputies executed during the Terror.

    Look for: On the river side, two tall rostral columns, decorated with ships’ prows, stand for commerce and navigation.

  • Pont de Pierre

    Bridge · 1822

    Napoleon ordered a bridge here, and it was finished in 1822. Its seventeen arches are often said to match the letters of Napoléon Bonaparte.

  • Water Mirror

    Waterfront · 2006

    It opened in 2006 as part of the riverfront redesign by landscape architect Michel Corajoud. Children splash across it on summer days.

    Look for: Crouch low at the river end and the whole Place de la Bourse appears upside down at your feet.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Bordeaux and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Bordeaux passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
